Version 0.3.0 keeps the pMOM regression and MRF selection model but replaces the
previous Laplace-based selection and conditional coefficient workflow with one
joint sampler. Its transition rules and summaries are described below. Exact
conditional calculations remove that Laplace approximation; finite MCMC error
and incomplete exploration remain possible.

# Joint target

Let s index availability subgroups, l platforms and j molecular features.
Write v_s for residual variance, z_s for the working response and A_s for active
coefficients, including the always-active intercept and clinical variables.
The sampler targets

\[
p(\Gamma,\beta,v,\Theta,z\mid D)
\propto p(D,z\mid\beta,v,\Gamma)
\prod_s p(\beta_{s,A_s}\mid v_s,\Gamma_s)p(v_s)
\prod_l p(\Gamma_l\mid\Theta_l)p(\Theta_l).
\]

The Gaussian working likelihood and first-order pMOM prior are

\[
z_s\mid\beta_s,v_s\sim N(X_s\beta_s,v_sI),
\qquad
p(\beta_{sj}\mid\gamma_{sj}=1,v_s)
=\frac{\beta_{sj}^2}{\tau_{sj}v_s}
\phi(\beta_{sj};0,\tau_{sj}v_s).
\]

An excluded molecular coefficient is exactly zero. Clinical coefficients and
the intercept also have pMOM priors but are always active. `imr_priors()` gives
molecular and forced coefficients separate scales. The inverse-gamma density
uses the shape/rate convention

\[
p(v_s)\propto v_s^{-a-1}\exp(-b/v_s).
\]

Binary models retain the variance parameter with shape and rate both 100,000,
anchoring it near one. This is not exactly the fixed-unit-variance probit model.

# Joint selection and coefficient updates

For feature j, hold the remaining coefficients and the variance fixed and set

\[
r_{sj}=z_s-\sum_{k\ne j}x_{sk}\beta_{sk},
\qquad
V_{sj}=\frac{v_s}{x_{sj}^{T}x_{sj}+1/\tau_{sj}},
\qquad
m_{sj}=\frac{x_{sj}^{T}r_{sj}}{x_{sj}^{T}x_{sj}+1/\tau_{sj}}.
\]

Multiplying the Gaussian likelihood by the pMOM prior and integrating this one
coefficient gives the conditional inclusion Bayes factor

\[
B_{sj}
=\sqrt{\frac{V_{sj}}{\tau_{sj}v_s}}
\exp\!\left(\frac{m_{sj}^2}{2V_{sj}}\right)
\frac{m_{sj}^2+V_{sj}}{\tau_{sj}v_s}.
\]

For a platform feature, the implementation updates its entire subgroup
selection pattern g together. Conditional pattern probabilities are

\[
P(\gamma_{lj}=g\mid\text{rest},D)
\propto
\exp\!\left\{\nu_l\mathbf1^Tg+g^T\Theta_lg
+\sum_s g_s\log B_{sj}\right\}.
\]

Enumeration covers the subgroups where that platform is available. The MRF
has at most 16 such subgroups in this implementation. BMS fixes interactions
to zero, so the pattern distribution factorizes into independent Bernoulli
probabilities. There are no birth/death boundary proposals in this update.

After choosing the pattern, each newly active coefficient is drawn from

\[
p(\beta_{sj}\mid\gamma_{sj}=1,\text{rest},D)
=\frac{\beta_{sj}^2\phi(\beta_{sj};m_{sj},V_{sj})}
{m_{sj}^2+V_{sj}}.
\]

The sampler also uses this conditional for forced coefficients. Rejection
sampling uses a mixture of a standard normal and a signed square root of a
chi-square variable with three degrees of freedom. If a=m/c and b=sqrt(V)/c,
where c=max(abs(m),sqrt(V)), the mixture probability for the normal component
is a²/(a²+b²), and a candidate u is accepted with probability

\[
\frac{(a+bu)^2}{2(a^2+b^2u^2)}.
\]

The inequality (a+bu)² ≤ 2(a²+b²u²) supplies a valid envelope. Both signs of
active coefficients can be visited; the sampler does not restrict effects to
be positive.

Whole-feature pair proposals help exchange highly correlated predictors. A
uniformly chosen feature pair swaps its complete subgroup selection patterns.
Within groups where inclusion changes, the proposed active coefficient is
sampled from its conditional distribution. Because all molecular features on
a platform share the same selection prior and scale, the MRF prior factors
cancel under this whole-column exchange. The acceptance ratio is the product
of new-to-old conditional Bayes factors across affected groups. This move
complements the pattern update; it does not guarantee adequate mixing for all
correlation structures.

# Variance, augmented responses and interactions

If d_s=|A_s| includes all active forced and molecular effects, the variance
conditional is

\[
v_s\mid\text{rest},D\sim IG\!\left(
 a+\frac{n_s}{2}+\frac{3d_s}{2},\quad
 b+\frac12\left[\|z_s-X_s\beta_s\|^2+
 \sum_{j\in A_s}\frac{\beta_{sj}^2}{\tau_{sj}}\right]\right).
\]

The additional 3d_s/2 follows from the pMOM density, including its Gaussian
normalizer. Replacing it with the Gaussian-prior expression changes the target.

Continuous responses are fixed. Binary latent responses are normal with mean
X_s beta_s and variance v_s, truncated above zero for outcome one and below
zero for outcome zero. Observed survival events are fixed at their working
response; censored responses are normal draws above the working censoring
bound. The default survival working response is log time. Tail calculations
use log probabilities without a fixed upper truncation constant.

Each IMR platform uses the normalized selection prior

\[
p(\Gamma_l\mid\Theta_l)
=Z_l(\Theta_l)^{-p_l}
\exp\!\left\{\nu_l\sum_j\mathbf1^T\gamma_{lj}
+\sum_j\gamma_{lj}^T\Theta_l\gamma_{lj}\right\},
\]

where p_l is its number of features and

\[
Z_l(\Theta_l)=\sum_{g\in\{0,1\}^{S_l}}
\exp\{\nu_l\mathbf1^Tg+g^T\Theta_lg\}.
\]

Theta_l is symmetric with zero diagonal, so a pair interaction enters the
quadratic form twice. Positive off-diagonal entries have independent Gamma
shape/rate priors. Proposals are normal random walks on log theta. The log
acceptance ratio contains the change in the normalized MRF density, the Gamma
prior and the proposal correction log(theta_new/theta_old). BMS stores no
interaction parameters.

# Stored draws and posterior summaries

Every retained iteration stores coefficients, variances, interactions and the
augmented joint log density. Augmented responses are optional. Selection
indicators are reconstructed from exact coefficient zeros, avoiding a duplicate
history. The log-density trace is a joint augmented-state density, not a
marginal model probability or a model-comparison score.

`posterior_draws()` preserves iteration, chain and parameter dimensions.
`coef()`, `summary()`, `confint()` and `predict()` use these same draws. All
reported quantiles use the empirical inverse CDF (type 1), with a small
floating-point tolerance at exact CDF boundaries. Selection-indicator endpoints
remain zero or one. They describe the indicator distribution, not Monte Carlo
uncertainty in an estimated inclusion probability.

Prediction averages Gaussian conditional means or binary conditional
probabilities over draws. Future-observation prediction also simulates residual
variation. Log-time survival predictions transform the posterior response
samples and report medians; a log-normal mixture need not have a finite mean.

# Diagnostics and validation boundaries

The package delegates rank-normalized split/folded R-hat, bulk/tail ESS and mean
MCSE to the [posterior package](https://mc-stan.org/posterior/reference/rhat.html).
Splitting an odd-length chain uses equally sized beginning and ending halves,
omitting its middle draw. Parameters constant within a chain cannot receive a
standard R-hat assessment. Such cases are identified explicitly, including
rare selection indicators and fixed observed event responses.

The maintained reference checks enumerate small selection spaces and integrate
coefficients, variances and interactions independently. Binary and censored
references integrate the observed-data likelihood and check quadrature
refinement. The cases cover Gaussian, binary, censored, strongly correlated
predictors, missing platforms and IMR/BMS. These checks assess the transition
target on tractable problems. Real-data chain diagnostics and stability must
still be examined for each analysis.

`cv_imr(..., cv_method = "refit")` reruns the full procedure in training folds.
The optional reweighting method uses the [loo PSIS implementation](https://mc-stan.org/loo/reference/psis.html)
on inverse held-out observed-data likelihoods and reports weight diagnostics.
It retains full-fit preprocessing, which must be considered when comparing it
with refit CV.

# Relationship to earlier results

The 2017 article specifies the statistical model; version 0.3.0 uses a new
joint inference algorithm. Archived implementations used Laplace model scores
and, in some versions, different MRF updates, prior indexing and CV rules.
Results from those versions are not interchangeable with a new joint fit.
Keep their original source and outputs when explaining historical numerical
differences. See [methods and reproducibility](https://h7nian.github.io/IntegMultiReg/method-coverage.html)
and the [migration guide](https://h7nian.github.io/IntegMultiReg/migration.html).
